# Lumen DSL — Layout, Sizing & Auto-Layout

Prefer **systematic** structure (auto-layout with consistent gaps) over hand-placed
`p(x,y)` coordinates. Hand placement is fine for a few absolute elements; it does
not survive content that varies by account/contact.

## Sizing tokens (the `s(w,h)` args)

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `<number>` | fixed canonical layout points (`pt`) |
| `hug` | size to fit content (use for text whose copy may vary) |
| `fill` | expand to fill the parent's available main-axis space |
| `fill(weight)` / `fill:weight` | weighted fill among siblings |
| `$token` | a `$space.*`/`$radius.*`-style dimension token |

Rules of thumb:
- Use `hug` height for any text that can wrap or vary.
- Use `fill` only inside a layout context that can resolve it (an `al` container,
  or a frame with a definite cross-axis).
- Keep text boxes **wide enough for the real copy**; a too-narrow box forces extra
  lines and triggers overflow (`LUMV0903`).
- Do not put `mm` or renderer-pixel thinking into child `p()`/`s()` values.
  Page/export declarations may use `px`, `mm`, `in`, or `pt`, but child geometry
  is authored in canonical layout points.

## Artboard-local layout

Page presets and explicit page sizes normalize into artboard layout bounds before
children are interpreted. The child coordinate space is always artboard-local or
parent-local:

- A4 portrait: about `595 x 842 pt`, with print metadata of `210mm x 297mm`.
- US Letter: `612 x 792 pt`, with print metadata of `8.5in x 11in`.
- `size(1080,1080,px)`: `1080 x 1080 pt`, with a `1080 x 1080 px` raste...

# Lumen DSL Vetted Block Catalog — Full-Artifact Compositions

These are complete, pre-proportioned **page** blocks. ASSEMBLE one of these for the
requested surface, then swap copy via the `#slot:` fixture lines — do not re-invent
proportions from primitives (that is what overcrowds designs and fails preflight on
`LUMV0810`/`LUMV0903`/`LUMV0904`). Every example below was personally run through
`.context/p02-validate.py` and returned `{"ok": true}` (the only warnings are
`LUMB0613`/`LUMB0614`, the platform-font-embedding warnings, which never fail a block).

Shared rules these blocks bake in (from the P0.2 spec §0–§5):

- **One clipped root `artboard` per page**, `s(fill,fill)`, background on its `fill(...)`. Never hardcode the root size.
- **Every personalizable text node is slotted** with a FIXED `s(W,…)` WIDTH sized for its worst_case, plus `wrap_text(true)` + a realistic `max_lines(N)`, and a `#slot:<key> sample(...) worst_case(...)` line under the page (the ONLY way fixtures attach). Use a **hug HEIGHT** (`s(W,hug)` / `s(fill,hug)`) so the box sizes to the actual lines and leaves no empty band — `max_lines(N)` still caps the line count. `text_fit` now uses the node's own line height, so hug heights validate for slotted nodes too (eyebrow/logo/name single-liners and headlines all hug). Non-personalized labels omit `slot(...)` and may use `hug`.
- **Centered labels use align(center) + hug height.** A label centered on BOTH axes by its parent (`al(…, x(c), y(c))` — a numeral in a circle chip, a stat numeral, a CTA button label) gets a standalone `align(center)` on the TEXT node so the glyph is centered (text-anchor=middle) INDEPENDENTLY of `style($type.x)`, plus a **hug height** so the parent's `y(c)` centers the actual glyph-tall box. Keep the label fill-width (`s(fill,hug) align(center)` for chip numerals/stat values AND CTA button labels) — `align(center)` centers the glyph inside that fill-width box; hug heights now validate for slotted nodes too (`text_fit` uses the node's own line height). NEVER use a hug WIDTH on a label (`s(hug,…)` is rejected by `LUMV0902`).
- **Width floors are large** (platform type is big). Calibrated facts used below: `$type.body` overflows a 499pt A4 column even for a 13-word sentence — **use `$type.body.small` for body copy at A4/postcard widths**. `$type.display` is too large for a 4-word headline even at 888pt wide / `max_lines(4)` — **use `$type.headline` for hero headlines**. A single over-wide word can blow `LUMV0810` at any height: at A4 width, "Recover **every** missed patient call." never fit; dropping a word to "Recover missed patient calls." (4 words) fits at `s(499,140) max_lines(2)`.
- **Content discipline = uncrowded.** One focal region; one CTA per artifact; headline 4-8 words `max_lines(2)`; subtitle 6-13 words `max_lines(3)`; benefit title ≤2 words `max_lines(1)` + description ≤12 words `max_lines(2)`; stat = one numeral + ≤2-word label. **Never 3 benefits across a portrait page — stack them vertically.** Smaller surfaces drop content rather than shrink it.

---

## Social square ad — header + hero + 3-up stat row + CTA + footer (1080×1080)

**When to use:** a square social/display ad (Instagram, LinkedIn square). The single
focal message with three proof stats and one CTA.

**When to use / Content budget:** `size(1080,1080,px)` → 1080×1080pt; `pad(96)` ⇒ 888pt
content column (~65% whitespace). Logo label + eyebrow in the header; hero headline 4-8
words `max_lines(2)` via `$type.headline` **stepped up to `font_size($type.size.7xl)` (80pt)**
at `s(888,hug)` — a 1080² canvas is far larger than A4, so the role's default 56 does NOT
dominate; the 7xl step makes the headline the clear focal point (80 vs the 48pt stats) while
the role still supplies weight/color (height hugs to the actual lines, `lh(1.04)` for the big
size). Subtitle ≤8 words `$type.body` `s(820,hug)` `max_lines(3)` (height hugs); three stats
each a `$type.stat` numeral `s(fill,hug)` + a ≤2-word `$type.body.small` label `s(270,hug)`;
one inverse-fill CTA `s(340,72)` whose fill-width label centers its glyph with `align(center)`
+ a hug height (`s(fill,hug)`). The URL caption hugs its height (`s(360,hug)`). **Distribution
(no dead bands):** the root is top-anchored (`y(s)`) with three children — a hug `header`, a
**`fill`-height `main` (`s(888,fill) y(c)`)** holding hero + stats, and a hug `footer`. `main`
absorbs all the vertical slack and centers hero + stats, so the header pins top, the footer is
pushed to the bottom, and the content sits centered in generous margin — NOT `y(sb)` with three
sparse bands (which strands each as a thin strip). Stat columns are fixed `s(270,…)` (270×3 + 2
gaps < 888), well above the ~160pt 2-word floor. Centered labels use align(center) + hug height;
text heights hug.

```text

  artboard al(v, x(s), y(s), g($space.section), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.brand) clip(true)
    header al(h, x(sb), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      brand al(h, x(s), y(c), g(12), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(360,hug)
        mark r p(0,0) s(40,40) fill($surface.inverse) rd($radius.badge)
        logo text "Insight Health" p(0,0) s(300,40) style($type.label) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.name)
      eyebrow text "FOR SPECIALTY CLINICS" p(0,0) s(420,36) style($type.eyebrow) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.eyebrow)
    main al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.section), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,fill)
      hero al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
        headline text "Answer every patient call." p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.headline) font_size($type.size.7xl) lh(1.04) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
        subtitle text "Insight Health answers, qualifies, and books visits." p(0,0) s(820,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(offer.primary_message)
      stats al(h, x(sb), y(s), g($space.lg), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
        s1 al(v, x(s), g(4), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(270,hug)
          s1v text "92%" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.stat) max_lines(1)
          s1l text "calls answered" p(0,0) s(270,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.3) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(stat.1.label)
        s2 al(v, x(s), g(4), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(270,hug)
          s2v text "3x" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.stat) max_lines(1)
          s2l text "faster booking" p(0,0) s(270,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.3) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(stat.2.label)
        s3 al(v, x(s), g(4), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(270,hug)
          s3v text "24/7" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.stat) max_lines(1)
          s3l text "live coverage" p(0,0) s(270,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.3) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(stat.3.label)
    footer al(h, x(sb), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      cta al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(18,36)) p(0,0) s(340,72) fill($surface.inverse) rd($radius.button)
        cta_text text "Book a Demo" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.cta) align(center) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta)
      url text "insighthealth.ai" p(0,0) s(360,hug) style($type.caption) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.url)
  #slot:account.name sample("Insight Health") worst_case("Insight Health Systems")
  #slot:campaign.eyebrow sample("FOR SPECIALTY CLINICS") worst_case("FOR SPECIALTY CLINICS")
  #slot:campaign.headline sample("Answer every patient call.") worst_case("Give your team their hours back.")
  #slot:offer.primary_message sample("Insight Health answers, qualifies, and books visits.") worst_case("Insight Health answers, qualifies, books the visit, and routes the rest.")
  #slot:stat.1.label sample("calls answered") worst_case("calls answered")
  #slot:stat.2.label sample("faster booking") worst_case("faster booking")
  #slot:stat.3.label sample("live coverage") worst_case("live coverage")
  #slot:campaign.cta sample("Book a Demo") worst_case("Book a Demo")
  #slot:account.url sample("insighthealth.ai") worst_case("insighthealth.ai")
```

## Full-canvas poster — sparse big-canvas ad, distributed (1080×1080)

**When to use:** a LIGHT-content big-canvas ad — one focal message + CTA, no proof
stats. This is the template to reach for whenever content is sparse on a tall/large
canvas, so it does NOT end up as three stranded strips with dead bands. It is the
"poster idiom" from `knowledge/design/foundations` made concrete.

**Distribution (the whole point):** the root is **top-anchored** (`y(s)`), NOT `y(sb)`,
with three children — a hug `header` (brand lockup), a **`fill`-height `main`
(`s(888,fill) y(c)`)** carrying the focal block (kicker + big headline + subtitle), and
a hug `footer` (CTA + url). `main` absorbs ALL the vertical slack and centers its
content, so the header pins to the top, the footer is pushed to the bottom, and the
message sits centered in generous margin — no mid-page voids. Hero headline stepped to
`font_size($type.size.7xl)` (80) so it dominates the 1080 canvas (the role default 56
would not). `$type.body` subtitle at `s(820,hug)` (wide square hero column). Add a proof
row inside `main` only if you genuinely have stats — otherwise keep it sparse.

```text
page poster_square size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(s), g($space.section), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    header al(h, x(s), y(c), g(12), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      mark al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(44,44) fill($surface.brand) rd($radius.badge)
        markt text "IH" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.eyebrow) max_lines(1)
      logo text "Insight Health AI" p(0,0) s(400,hug) style($type.label) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.name)
    main al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,fill)
      kicker text "PRODUCT LAUNCH" p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.eyebrow) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.eyebrow)
      headline text "Meet Magic-Doc." p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.headline) font_size($type.size.7xl) lh(1.04) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
      subtitle text "Automate healthcare document processing at one-tenth the cost." p(0,0) s(820,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(offer.primary_message)
    footer al(h, x(sb), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      cta al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(18,36)) p(0,0) s(300,72) fill($surface.brand) rd($radius.button)
        cta_text text "Book a Demo" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.cta) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta)
      url text "insighthealth.ai" p(0,0) s(320,hug) style($type.caption) align(right) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.url)
  #slot:account.name sample("Insight Health AI") worst_case("Insight Health Systems")
  #slot:campaign.eyebrow sample("PRODUCT LAUNCH") worst_case("PRODUCT LAUNCH")
  #slot:campaign.headline sample("Meet Magic-Doc.") worst_case("Introducing Magic-Doc.")
  #slot:offer.primary_message sample("Automate healthcare document processing at one-tenth the cost.") worst_case("Automate healthcare document processing for clinics and hospitals at one-tenth the cost.")
  #slot:campaign.cta sample("Book a Demo") worst_case("Book a Demo")
  #slot:account.url sample("insighthealth.ai") worst_case("insighthealth.ai")

## Image hero — full-bleed photo + scrim + headline, brand top / message bottom (1080×1350)

**When to use:** an **editorial hero/poster** where a real **photo** carries the message —
a case study, a brand story, a product-in-context shot. Reach for this **only when a photo
does real work** (see `knowledge/images/decide`); a clean typographic layout beats a
gratuitous stock image. The canonical "text over a hero photo" idiom.

**The scrim rule (non-negotiable):** a full-bleed `image` fills the clipped artboard, a
**dark scrim rect** (`fill($surface.inverse) o($opacity.scrim)` = 0.56) sits over it, and
**inverse-fill text** (`fill($text.inverse)`) sits over the scrim — so the headline stays
legible on a busy photo. **Declaration order is z-order:** image → scrim → content. Without
the scrim, text on a photo is illegible the moment the image is busy, and the imagery critic
gates it (legibility-over-image is a hard axis). When the copy can instead sit on its own
solid band, the split layout needs no scrim — see `knowledge/images/placement` Idiom B.

**The artboard declares `fill($surface.inverse)` — and that is load-bearing, not
decoration.** Brand tokens resolve **relative to their container's surface**: on a dark
artboard `$text.inverse` / `$type.*` ink resolves to **light** (white) so it reads over the
scrim; on a light `$surface.page` artboard the *same* tokens resolve **dark** and the
headline goes invisible against the dark photo. The dark fill is also the correct fallback
colour if the image ever fails to load. So a full-bleed-photo surface is a **dark surface** —
keep the artboard `$surface.inverse`.

**Placement is on the node, not the DSL line.** The `image` line carries only
`asset(hero_photo)` — its **`fit:cover` + focal point + alt** are set on the node's
AssetPlacement by the agent's `asset(action="place")` tool (or the editor inspector), the same
`place_asset_in_node` op a human edit issues. **Aspect comes from the 1080×1350 frame**, so the photo is cropped to
fill, never stretched. Swap `hero_photo` for the generated/uploaded asset id.

**Distribution:** the `content` autolayout fills the frame at `y(sb)` (space-between) with
two children — a hug **brand** lockup and a hug **copy** block — so the brand pins to the
top, the message pins to the bottom, and the photo + scrim fill the band behind. Hero
headline ≤5 words `max_lines(2)` stepped to `font_size($type.size.6xl)` (64) so it dominates
the 1080 canvas; kicker ≤2 words; subtitle ≤8 words `max_lines(2)`; one inverse CTA whose
fill-width label centers its glyph with `align(center)` + a hug height. Centered labels use
align(center) + hug height; text heights hug.

```text
page hero_image size(1080,1350,px)
  artboard fr p(0,0) s(fill,fill) clip(true) fill($surface.inverse)
    photo image asset(hero_photo) p(0,0) s(1080,1350)
    scrim r p(0,0) s(1080,1350) fill($surface.inverse) o($opacity.scrim)
    content al(v, x(s), y(sb), g($space.section), pad(80)) p(0,0) s(1080,1350)
      brand al(h, x(s), y(c), g(12), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(920,hug)
        mark r p(0,0) s(40,40) fill($surface.accent) rd($radius.badge)
        logo text "Insight Health" p(0,0) s(360,hug) style($type.label) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.name)
      copy al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(920,hug)
        kicker text "CASE STUDY" p(0,0) s(920,hug) style($type.eyebrow) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.eyebrow)
        headline text "Faster triage, calmer clinics." p(0,0) s(920,hug) style($type.headline) font_size($type.size.6xl) lh(1.06) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
        subtitle text "How Northside cut missed calls to near zero." p(0,0) s(820,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(offer.primary_message)
        cta al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(18,36)) p(0,0) s(320,72) fill($surface.inverse) rd($radius.button)
          cta_text text "Read the story" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.cta) align(center) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta)
  #slot:account.name sample("Insight Health") worst_case("Insight Health Systems")
  #slot:campaign.eyebrow sample("CASE STUDY") worst_case("CASE STUDY")
  #slot:campaign.headline sample("Faster triage, calmer clinics.") worst_case("Faster triage, calmer clinics.")
  #slot:offer.primary_message sample("How Northside cut missed calls to near zero.") worst_case("How Northside cut missed calls to near zero.")
  #slot:campaign.cta sample("Read the story") worst_case("Read the story")
```

## A4 one-pager — header + hero + vertical 3-up benefit list + CTA footer (A4 portrait)

**When to use:** a printed/PDF one-pager (sell sheet, leave-behind). Header brand row,
a hero statement, three benefits, and a CTA footer.

**When to use / Content budget:** `preset(a4,portrait)` → 595×842pt; `pad(48)` ⇒ 499pt
content width and ~746pt of vertical room. **Stack the three benefits as full-width
rows — never 3 across on A4** (3×220pt of descriptions > 595pt page width ⇒ guaranteed
`LUMV0810`). Each benefit row = number chip `s(56,56)` + `g(20)` + a `s(423,hug)` text
column (56+20+423 = 499); the chip's numeral centers its glyph with `align(center)` + a hug
height (`s(fill,hug)`) so the chip's `x(c),y(c)` centers the actual glyph instead of a tall
box, and the title/description heights hug (`s(423,hug)`) so short copy reserves no empty
band. Hero headline ≤4 words at A4 width — `$type.headline` `s(499,hug) max_lines(2)`
("Recover missed patient calls."; note "Recover **every**…" does NOT fit at 499 — drop the
over-wide word; the headline height hugs to the actual lines). Lead uses
**`$type.body.small`** at `s(499,hug) max_lines(3)` (height hugs) because `$type.body`
overflows a 499pt column. Tight single-line labels hug their height too (eyebrow
`s(499,hug)`, logo `s(230,hug)`); the tag/contact captions hug (`s(209,hug)`/`s(219,hug)`).
**Distribution (no truncated bottom):** hero + benefit list are wrapped in a
**`fill`-height `main` (`s(499,fill) y(s)`)** between a hug `header` and a hug `footer`.
`main` absorbs the vertical slack and flows its content from the top, so the **footer
is pinned to the page bottom** (verified: footer bottom = 794 = page − pad) — the page
reads as a complete framed layout, NOT content stopping at 60% with an empty lower half.
Use `y(s)` (top-flow) for a multi-section sell-sheet like this; for a SPARSE single-block
portrait card, center the block instead (`main … y(c)`). The whole page is gapped with
`$space.stack.loose` between regions. (`LUMV0801` may appear as a non-fatal *warning* —
it does not fail the block; content fits within bounds.) Centered labels use align(center)
+ hug height; text heights hug.

```text
page onepager_a4 preset(a4,portrait)
  artboard al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.loose), pad(48)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    header al(h, x(sb), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,hug)
      brand al(h, x(s), y(c), g(10), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(280,hug)
        mark r p(0,0) s(32,32) fill($surface.brand) rd($radius.badge)
        logo text "Insight Health" p(0,0) s(230,hug) style($type.label) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.name)
      tag text "Intake, automated" p(0,0) s(209,hug) style($type.caption) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.tagline)
    main al(v, x(s), y(s), g($space.stack.loose), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,fill)
      hero al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.tight), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,hug)
        eyebrow text "FOR SPECIALTY CLINICS" p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.eyebrow) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.eyebrow)
        headline text "Recover missed patient calls." p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.12) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
        subtitle text "Insight Health answers, qualifies, and books visits for your front desk." p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(offer.primary_message)
      list al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,hug)
        r1 al(h, x(s), y(s), g(20), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,hug)
          n1 al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(56,56) fill($surface.brand.subtle) rd($radius.full)
            n1t text "1" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.subtitle) align(center) max_lines(1)
          t1 al(v, x(s), g(6), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(423,hug)
            t1t text "Faster intake" p(0,0) s(423,hug) style($type.subtitle) lh(1.15) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(benefit.1.title)
            t1d text "Answer and route every patient call in seconds, day or night." p(0,0) s(423,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(benefit.1.desc)
        r2 al(h, x(s), y(s), g(20), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,hug)
          n2 al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(56,56) fill($surface.brand.subtle) rd($radius.full)
            n2t text "2" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.subtitle) align(center) max_lines(1)

## Adapting these blocks (keep them valid)

- **Re-skin via slots only.** Edit the `#slot:` `sample`/`worst_case` lines; keep each
  slotted node's fixed `s(W,…)` WIDTH unless the worst_case grows — if it does, re-validate.
- **Centered labels use align(center) + hug height; text heights hug.** A label centered on
  both axes by its parent (`x(c),y(c)`) gets a standalone `align(center)` on the TEXT node so
  the glyph is centered, plus a hug height (`s(fill,hug) align(center)` for chip numerals/stat
  values AND CTA labels) so `y(c)` centers the glyph-tall box, not a dead zone. Slotted body
  text uses a hug height (`s(W,hug)`/`s(fill,hug)`) so short copy reserves no empty band — and
  `text_fit` now uses the node's own line height, so hug heights validate for slotted nodes too
  (eyebrow, logo/name, headlines all hug). Never use a `hug` WIDTH on a label (`LUMV0902`); keep
  it fill-width or fixed-width and let `align(center)` center the glyph.
- **Headline width trap.** At the narrower surfaces (A4 499pt, flyer 620pt, postcard
  368pt) a single over-wide word can overflow `LUMV0810` at any height. Shorten the
  headline (fewer/shorter words), do not just add height or `max_lines`.
- **Body copy at print widths uses `$type.body.small`, not `$type.body`.** `$type.body`
  overflows columns ≤ ~620pt. Reserve `$type.body` for the wide square hero (`s(820,…)`).
- **Hero headlines use `$type.headline`; step the SIZE per surface.** The role's default
  size (56) is tuned for A4 — keep it on A4/postcard. On a large canvas it does not
  dominate, so step the size with a token: `font_size($type.size.6xl)` (64) for a landscape
  flyer, `font_size($type.size.7xl)` (80) for a 1080² square. The role still gives
  weight/color; only the size changes, and it stays a fixed value (editor-safe). Do NOT
  switch to `$type.display` for this — it carries display *styling* and still can't fit a
  4-word line at 888 wide. The rule: **one element dominates; the hero reads visibly larger
  than any stat/secondary value** (see `knowledge/design/foundations`).
- **Do not add a third tier of content to the postcard or flyer.** They are short
  surfaces; the validator's `LUMV0801` bounds check will reject an extra band. Stay with
  one focal message + one secondary region + one CTA.
```

# Brand Kits — Using & Generating

A Brand Kit is the resolvable design system a scene references through `$tokens`.
Lumen designs look on-brand because they reference role tokens, not because the
model guessed nice values.

## Using a kit (authoring)

Use tokens when the design should adapt to an uploaded, generated, or platform
default kit:

```text
fill($surface.brand)     fill($surface.card)
stroke($border.default,$stroke.width.firm)
g($space.stack.default)  pad($space.card.padding)
rd($radius.card)
style($type.headline)    style($type.body)
```

If a scene contains token references, preflight must receive an effective Brand
Kit. The platform default kit is valid when the user supplied none. The DSL
compiler lowers token refs into scene token carriers where a precise field exists;
Brand Kit resolution and fallback happen in preflight. Avoid ambiguous tokenized
forms with no precise carrier (e.g. tokenizing only the size arg of `font(...)`) —
prefer a full `style($type.headline)`.

See `token-taxonomy.md` for the role groups and the product-ready minimum set.

- approval status: `draft`, `generated_unreviewed`, `approved`, `deprecated`
- a `medium` mode for digital vs print behavior (see `modes.md`)
- logo and reusable brand-asset rules (see `logo-and-assets.md`)
- strict scene governance diagnostics (see `brand-validation.md`)
- compatibility reports between kit versions

snippets.excerpt:
# Lumen DSL — Grammar Reference

The compact, precise reference for the Lumen DSL surface. DSL text compiles into
canonical `Scene` operations. It is line-oriented and indentation-sensitive.

## Line shapes

```
line       = indent , ( checkpoint | comment | page | element | directive | modify )
indent     = { "  " }                 # exactly two spaces per level
checkpoint = "//" text                # labeled history anchor
comment    = "#"  text                # ignored (note: a leading "#ref" is a modify line, not a comment)
page       = "page" id [ page_property* ]
element    = id kind property*  |  kind id property*    # either order
directive  = verb "(" args ")"        # delete / parent / clone / replace / ungroup / …
modify     = "#" ref property*        # targeted edit of an existing object
```

Rules: two spaces per indent level (`LUMD0301`); never indent more than one level
deeper than the parent (`LUMD0302`); only containers may hold children
(`LUMD0304`); `page` lines must be top-level (`LUMD0305`).

## Page header

```text
page page_a4 preset(a4,portrait)          # preset(name, orientation?)
page story size(1080,1920,px)             # size(width, height, unit)
```

- Presets: `a4`, `us_letter`, `linkedin_ad`, `envelope_dl`, `custom`
  (unknown → `LUMD0223`). Orientation: `portrait` | `landscape` (unknown →
  `LUMD0224`); A4/Letter default portrait, ad/envelope default landscape.
- Units: `px`, `mm`, `in`/`inch`, `pt` (unknown → `LUMD0252`). Dimensions must
  be positive (`LUMD0251`). `size(...)` needs all three args (`LUMD0250`).
  New page commands normalize to canonical `pt` artboard bounds while preserving
  the requested source/export size.
- Presets are shortcuts only. **Never fake a square ad as a square frame inside an
  A4 page** — set the page size.
- Child `p()`/`s()` values are authored in canonical layout points and are
  artboard- or parent-local. Do not use physical `mm` or renderer pixels for
  child coordinates.

## Node kinds

Containers (may have children): `frame`/`fr`, `group`/`gr`, `autolayout`/`al`.
Leaves (no children, `LUMD0304` if nested): `rect`/`r`, `ellipse`/`e`/`c`,
`line`/`l`, `text`/`t`, `image`/`img`, `vector`/`v`, `svg`, `instance`/`inst`.

```text
hero fr p(0,0) s(595,160) fill(#ffffff) rd(16)
  title text "Welcome" p(24,24) s(440,hug) font("Inter",28,700,left)
```

Unknown kind → `LUMD0206`. Duplicate node id → `LUMD0401`. Node outside a
page/container → `LUMD0402`. `image` needs `asset(id)` (`LUMD0403`); `vector`
needs `path("…")` (`LUMD0404`); `instance` needs `source(id)` (`LUMD0405`).

## Property catalogue

Geometry and box:

| Property | Arity | Meaning |
|----------|-------|---------|
| `p(x,y)` | 2 | position in canonical layout points (`pt`), local to the parent/artboard |
| `s(w,h)` / `s(w,h,unit)` | 2–3 | size in canonical layout points; `w`/`h` are a number, `hug`, `fill`, `fill(weight)`, `fill:weight`, or `$token` |
| `rd(r)` / `radius(r)` | **1** | uniform corner radius — **4-arg per-corner is NOT supported** (→ `LUMD0230`) |
| `o(a)` / `opacity(a)` | 1 | node opacity |
| `rot(deg)` / `rotation(deg)` | 1 | rotation |
| `sk(x,y)` / `skew(x,y)` | 2 | skew |
| `flip(axis)` | 1 | `x`/`horizontal`, `y`/`vertical`, `both`/`xy`, `none` |
| `clip(bool)` | 1 | clip children |

Paint and effects (see `colors.md` and `skills/effects`):

| Property | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `fill(paint)` | single fill |
| `f[(id,paint),(paint),…]` | ordered fill stack |
| `background(paint)` / `bg(paint)` | page/container background |
| `stroke(paint,width)` or extended `stroke(id?,paint,w(),dash(),cap(),join(),align())` | stroke |
| `shadow(color,o(),x(),y(),blur(),spread())` or `shadow(x,y,blur[,spread],color)` | drop shadow |

Text (see `text.md`):

`text("…")`/`content`, `font("family",size,weight,align)` or `font($type.x)`,
`font_size(n)` or `font_size($type.size.x)` (step token overrides the role's
default size for big canvases — see `text.md`), `font_weight`, `style($type.x)`,
`align(left|center|right|justify)`
(standalone horizontal align; pairs with `style($type.x)`), `lh`, `ls`, `tracking`,
`wrap_text(bool)`, `max_lines(n)`, `dir(ltr|rtl|auto)`.

Auto-layout (on `al` containers; see `layout.md`):

`al(v|h, x(anchor), y(anchor), g(gap), pad(...), grow(n), wrap(bool))` where
anchor ∈ `start`/`s`, `center`/`c`, `end`/`e`, `space_between`/`sb`,
`stretch`/`st`.

Slots / ABM (see `knowledge/design-systems`):

`slot(key)`, `label("…")`, `required(bool)`, `placeholder("…")`, `sample("…")`,
`worst_case("…")`, `bind(node)`, `unbind(node)`.

Assets / vectors: `asset(id)`, `path("…")`, `source(node)`, `to(x,y)` (line end).

Any other property name → `LUMD0212 unknown property`. A property used on the
wrong node kind warns (e.g. `font(...)` on a non-text node → `LUMD0601`).

## Images, icons & the scrim idiom

Three ways to put a picture on a surface — pick by content (see `knowledge/images/decide`):

| Kind | DSL | Lowers to | Use for |
|------|-----|-----------|---------|
| raster image | `image asset(id)` / `img(id)` | `Image{asset_id,alt}` | a generated/uploaded photo, product, texture |
| library icon | `svg(icon:name)` | `Vector` (viewBox-fit, recolorable) | iconographic marks — `knowledge/images/icons` |
| hand vector  | `vector path("…")` / `v(…)` | `Vector` (node-local coords) | a bespoke path you author by hand |

**Fit / focal / alt are placement, not DSL leaf props.** An `image` line carries only
`asset(id)` (+ geometry/`slot`). The *cover/contain/crop fit*, the *focal point*, and the
*alt text* live on the node's **AssetPlacement**, attached by the agent's
`asset(action="place")` tool (or the editor's image inspector) — the same canonical
`place_asset_in_node` / `place_asset_in_slot` ops a human edit issues. So the DSL author **composes the frame +
image + scrim structure**; the placement is set on the node, not typed as a property on
the `image` line (`fit(...)`/`focal(...)` are not DSL properties). The default is
**`fit:cover` + a sensible focal point**; aspect comes from the *frame*, never stretch.

### The scrim idiom — text over an image is ALWAYS scrimmed

The blessed pattern is a **clipped frame holding the image, a sibling scrim rect, then the
text** — declaration order is z-order (image, scrim, text). The scrim is a semi-transparent
rect between the image and the text so the headline stays legible on a busy photo. Use
`$opacity.scrim` (0.56) or `$opacity.overlay` (0.88); a dark scrim (`$surface.inverse`)
under light text (`$text.inverse`). This is the single most common imagery failure the
critic gates — never put text on a photo without it.

**Give the frame `fill($surface.inverse)` (a dark surface).** Brand tokens resolve relative
to their container's surface, so a dark frame is what makes `$text.inverse` / the `$type.*`
roles resolve to **light** ink over the scrim — on a light (`$surface.page`) frame the same
tokens resolve dark and the headline vanishes against the photo. It is also the fallback
colour if the image fails to load.

```text
frame fr p(0,0) s(1080,1350) clip(true) rd($radius.card) fill($surface.inverse)
  photo image asset(hero_photo) p(0,0) s(1080,1350)          # cover-fit + focal set by asset(action="place")
  scrim r p(0,0) s(1080,1350) fill($surface.inverse) o($opacity.scrim)
  caption text "Faster triage, calmer clinics" p(64,1120) s(936,180) style($type.headline) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2)
```

When the text sits on its own solid band instead of on the photo, **no scrim is needed** —
see `knowledge/images/placement` (Idiom B) and the image-bearing block in
`knowledge/design/blocks/patterns`. For prompt-craft see `knowledge/images/prompts`.

## Two ways to change an existing scene

1. **Continuation** — append new nested element lines under an existing container
   (do not re-declare the page).
2. **Modify line** — `#<ref> prop(...)` edits an existing object in place. Refs:
   `#node_id`, `#page:id`, `#slot:key`, `#asset:id`, `#export:name`, `#document`.
   ```text
   #headline s(440,hug) font_size(22)      # resize + shrink one node
   #card s(400,520)                        # make the card taller to fix overflow
   ```

See `directives.md` for modify/delete/parent/clone/replace and
`diagnostics.md` for the full code map.

# Lumen DSL — Text & Typography

Text is the most common source of overflow. Measurement is real (server-side
SkParagraph shaping over the bundled Inter), so a box that the compiler says is
too small genuinely is.

## Properties

| Property | Aliases | Meaning |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `text("…")` | `content` | the string content |
| `font("family",size,weight,align)` | — | full type spec; align ∈ `left`/`center`/`right`/`justify` |
| `font($type.x)` | — | one typography token (preferred when branded) |
| `style($type.x)` | `text_style` | typography role token (preferred when branded) |
| `align(left\|center\|right\|justify)` | `text_align` | horizontal alignment, standalone — pairs with `style($type.x)` (which carries no align) |
| `font_size(n)` / `font_size($type.size.x)` | `font-size` | size only — a raw number OR a size-step token (the token form is preferred; see below) |
| `font_weight(n)` | `font-weight` | alias — weight only |
| `lh(n)` | `line_height` | line height multiplier |
| `ls(n)` | `letter_spacing` | pixel letter spacing |
| `tracking(n)` | — | design-tool tracking; `tracking(200)` ≈ `0.2em`, not 200px |
| `wrap_text(bool)` | `text_wrap` | enable wrapping |
| `max_lines(n)` | `max` | cap line count (>0; else `LUMD0255`); overflow → `LUMV0904` |
| `dir(ltr|rtl|auto)` | `direction` | base direction |

Canonical vs alias: prefer `font(...)` / `style($type.x)` / `lh(...)` / `ls(...)`
in new designs. `font_size`/`font_weight`/`tracking` are compatibility aliases for
*targeted text repairs* when a model has drifted into CSS/design-tool language.

`align(...)` is the horizontal alignment knob. Use it **standalone** alongside
`style($type.x)` — the style token carries no alignment — to center a label without
resizing its box: e.g. a numeral in a circle chip or a CTA label is
`style($type.cta) align(center)`. (It is also the 4th arg of `font(...)`.) To center
a label in a chip/button, the box does NOT need to hug the glyph — `align(center)`
centers the glyph within whatever width the box has. Vertical centering is an
auto-layout `y(c)` on the parent plus a hug height on the label (see `layout.md`);
there is no `valign`.

## Type-size scale — pick the step for the surface

A role (`style($type.headline)`) bakes in **one** size, tuned for a document-scale
page (A4 ≈ 595pt wide). On a much larger canvas (a 1080² social square, a wide
flyer) that same size is too small to dominate — the headline reads at the same
weight as a stat and the squint test fails. Fix it at the source: keep the role
for weight/color/line-height and **override the size with a step token**:

```
$type.size.xs=12  sm=14  md=16  lg=20  xl=24  2xl=32  3xl=36
$type.size.4xl=40 (hero)  5xl=48 (large hero)  6xl=64 (display)
$type.size.7xl=80  8xl=96  9xl=128  (oversize / display)
```

```text
# A4 / document scale — the role default is right, no override needed
headline text "Your appointment is confirmed." s(fill,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.08) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2)

# 1080² social hero — same role, but step the size up so it dominates
headline text "Meet Magic-Doc." s(fill,hug) style($type.headline) font_size($type.size.7xl) lh(1.08) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2)
```

The step token resolves to a fixed value regardless of canvas (no auto-scaling —
a human editor can resize it freely), and it wins over the role's default size.
**Rules of thumb** (canvas-independent): one element dominates per artifact; the
hero is ~2–3× body; a stat/secondary value must read *visibly smaller* than the
hero (don't let `$type.stat`, 48, rival a 56 headline — step the headline to
64–80 on a big canvas). See `knowledge/design/foundations`.

## Patterns that fit

```text
headline text "Let neurosurgeons focus on surgery." p(64,88) s(620,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.08) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2)
body     text "Insight Health handles calls, scheduling, and patient routing." p(64,240) s(600,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.35) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3)
cta_text text "Book a Demo" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.cta) max_lines(1)
```

- `hug` height so the box grows with the copy.
- Box **wide enough** for the real sentence.
- `wrap_text(true)` on anything that can vary.
- `max_lines(...)` so overflow is diagnosed early rather than clipping silently.
- `lh` for hierarchy: tight headlines (`1.05`–`1.15`), relaxed body (`1.3`–`1.45`).

### Text over an image

A headline or label placed **over a photo** must sit on a **scrim** and use an inverse
fill so it stays legible on a busy image: `style($type.headline) fill($text.inverse)`
over a sibling scrim rect (`fill($surface.inverse) o($opacity.scrim)`). Declaration order
is image → scrim → text. See the scrim idiom in `grammar.md` and
`knowledge/images/placement`; legibility-over-image is a hard imagery-critic gate.

## Patterns that overflow

```text
headline text "Very long headline that cannot fit" p(40,40) s(300,24) font("Inter",64,800,left)
body     text "A long paragraph forced into a tiny fixed box" p(40,120) s(300,24) font("Inter",18,400,left)
```

A fixed `24px` height with a 64px font, or a paragraph in a narrow box, will fail
fit validation (`LUMV0903 exceeds available height`, `LUMV0810 fixture overflows`).
The fix is small and targeted: widen/heighten the box, raise `max_lines`, drop the
font a point, or switch the slot's overflow policy to shrink/wrap. **Do not redesign
the whole scene to fix one box** — see `skills/repair-design`.

snippets.title: Design Foundations
snippets.excerpt:
# Design Foundations

Core judgment for every build — the taste rubric the visual critic scores against.
Load this for every design task. For DSL syntax see `knowledge/lumen-dsl/grammar`
+ `text`; for ready-made proportions see `knowledge/design/blocks`.

## Before you build

Read the intent. A vague prompt is the user evaluating you — deliver one tight,
impressive piece. A specific product prompt — clarity and usability come before
style. Either way, commit to a system first: a surface, 3–6 token roles with one
brand color, a type scale, a spacing rhythm. Then decide the ONE focal point and
the personality. Assemble from `blocks/` — don't invent proportions per run.

## Composition — one thing dominates

- **One dominant region per artifact.** Every screen needs a single element the
  eye lands on first; everything else is visibly subordinate (smaller, lighter,
  lower contrast). **Squint test:** if you blur the design and nothing pops, the
  hierarchy has failed — raise the contrast or the size gap.
- **Scale the hero to the surface.** Type sizes are fixed values, not
  canvas-relative — so the same `$type.headline` (56) that dominates an A4 page is
  lost on a 1080² canvas. Keep the role, step the size with a token:
  `font_size($type.size.6xl)` (64) for a landscape flyer, `7xl` (80) for a 1080²
  square (see `knowledge/lumen-dsl/text`). The hero must read **visibly larger than
  any `$type.stat` (48) or secondary value** — a stat that rivals the headline
  inverts the hierarchy.
- **Jump rule.** A heading is ~150–200% of body; the hero is ~2–3× body. Build
  hierarchy with **size + weight + color together**, not one alone.
- **Whitespace is margin, not gaps.** Aim for ~60–70% empty space, but it must
  read as generous margin *around a coherent block* — not as dead bands trapped
  *between* scattered elements. Then ask what to remove.
- **One alignment spine.** Pick a left (or center) edge and align everything to it;
  a single consistent spine reads as intentional. Don't mix left- and center-
  alignment in the same column. One CTA per section.
- **Information on surfaces over boxes.** Favor type/color hierarchy over boxing
  everything in cards; favor asymmetry and scale contrast over grid-like sameness.

## Distribute the canvas — no dead bands

A tall canvas with light content fails when the agent **start-stacks** everything
(empty bottom, "reads truncated") or spreads it with `y(sb)` so each region floats
alone (two empty bands, "disconnected strips"). Free space must read as *margin
around an anchored block*, never as gaps *between* stranded strips. The root
`artboard` is already a fixed-height frame (`s(fill,fill)`), so free vertical space
is real and must be claimed — by **alignment + a `fill`-height region**, never a
filler element.

- **Never make an empty spacer frame.** Express free space with sizing/alignment.
- **`y(sb)` (space-between) is for exactly TWO anchored blocks** (header top + footer
  bottom). With 3+ light blocks it scatters the slack into dead bands — don't.
- **The poster idiom (one focal block on a big canvas):** a `fill`-height content
  region absorbs the slack and centers its content; the header pins top and the
  footer is pushed to the bottom. Verified: header `y=96`, footer `y=944`, hero
  centered `y=500` on a 1080² canvas.
  ```text
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(s), g($space.section), pad(96)) s(fill,fill)
    header ...                       s(888,hug)          # pins top
    main   al(v, x(s), y(c), ...)    s(888,fill)         # ABSORBS slack, centers
      <eyebrow / headline / subtitle / proof — the focal block>
    footer al(h, x(sb), y(c), ...)   s(888,hug)          # pushed to bottom
  ```
- **Decision rule for light content on a big canvas** — choose by block count, never
  by manufacturing filler copy:
  - **One focal block** → put it in a `s(W,fill)` / `s(fill,fill)` region with `y(c)`;
    the empty area becomes symmetric margin.
  - **Two anchored blocks** (header/footer) → `y(sb)` on the fixed-height parent.
  - **A genuinely long page** → stack sections with a small inter-section gap and let
    each section own its vertical `pad()`; a focal middle region can still be `fill`.
- **Never strand a header alone over a void, and never leave the bottom of a
  fixed-height page empty.** If the body doesn't reach the page bottom, give it a
  `fill`-height region (stretch) or center it with `y(c)`. If the artifact genuinely
  lacks content for its surface (e.g. an appointment card with no date/time/location),
  add the real missing content — that is the honest fill, not a spacer.
- **Portrait pages (A4, posters) use the SAME idiom.** Wrap the body in a `s(W,fill)`
  `main` between a hug header and a hug footer so the footer pins to the page bottom
  and the page reads complete (not "truncated at 60%"). Pick `main`'s anchor by content
  DENSITY, not section count: use `y(s)` only when the content nearly **fills** the
  page (flows from the top, just a small margin above the pinned footer); use `y(c)`
  when the content is **sparse** so the focal group centers and the slack splits into
  small top+bottom margins — or distribute the sections with larger gaps so they fill.
  The failure to avoid: top-flowing sparse content so the footer (and a large band)
  floats empty below it — a sparse multi-section card still needs `y(c)`, not `y(s)`.

## Color & contrast

- **60-30-10:** one dominant surface (~60%), one secondary (~30%), one accent
  (~10%). The accent is the brand color — reserve it for the focal point / CTA.
- **Legibility is non-negotiable:** body text ≥ 4.5:1 against its surface, large
  text ≥ 3:1 (WCAG AA). Token resolution already corrects text color for its
  surface, but don't place a low-contrast accent as body copy.

## Avoid the AI clichés

- **Eyebrows:** the tinted pill above the headline is the #1 tell. Vary it — a
  plain overline, a short accent rule + label, or none. Reserve the pill for a
  genuine status badge ("NOW IN BETA").
- **Color:** skip blue→purple gradients, neon-on-dark, all-white-with-one-safe-
  accent, and low-opacity circles drifting behind sections.
- **Layout:** avoid three equal cards in a row as the default answer; avoid
  centering everything; avoid a lonely small headline stranded in a sea of white.
  If you've seen the move in three AI designs, drop it.

## Content budget (keeps it uncrowded — and keeps worst_case fixtures in the box)

Eyebrow 2–4 words; headline 4–8 words `max_lines(2)`; subtitle 6–13 words
`max_lines(3)`; body 12–25 words; benefit title ≤2 words; benefit description ≤12
words; one CTA label 2–3 words; stat = one numeral + ≤2-word label. If content
exceeds the budget, **drop it or stack vertically — never shrink type or cram more
in.** Smaller surfaces carry *less* content, not the same content smaller.

snippets.title: Imagery — Decide First (generate only what you can't build)
snippets.excerpt:
# Imagery — Decide First (generate only what you can't build)

The guardrail against gratuitous AI imagery. BEFORE generating or placing anything,
answer two questions: **does this surface need imagery at all**, and **if so, what
role** — which decides the *mechanism*. An image must earn its place by serving the
message; decoration that just fills space makes the design worse, not better. For how
to prompt see `knowledge/images/prompts`; for how to place + scrim see
`knowledge/images/placement`; for the available library icons see `knowledge/images/icons`.

## The decision table — content → mechanism

Route by what the content actually is. Most of these are NOT a generated photo.

| Content | Mechanism | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Photo, product shot, portrait, food, place/scene, **texture**, raster illustration | **`asset(action="generate_image")`** (text-to-image) | Only a model can render real photographic/painted content. |
| **Icon, pictogram, simple flat illustration, logo glyph** | **icon/library** — `svg(icon:name)` or a brand `logo.*`/`asset.icon.*` token (logo roles + allowed surfaces: `knowledge/design-systems/logo-and-assets`) | A curated vector is reliable, crisp at any size, and recolorable; a model garbles small flat marks. NOT `asset(action="generate_image")`. |
| Abstract / decorative geometric, accents | **shapes + gradients** (`r`, `vector`, gradient fills) | Built primitives are sharper, on-brand, and free. |
| Flat color field, brand block, panel | **solid / gradient fill** (`fill($surface.*)`) | A token surface, not an image. |
| Data, comparison, timeline, process, metrics | **layout / data-display blocks**, not imagery | Information belongs on surfaces, not behind a photo. |

## Does it need an image at all? Default to NO

Most enterprise one-pagers, cards, and slides are **stronger as clean typographic
layouts** with a strong hero headline, generous whitespace, and one accent. Reach for
a photo only when it does real work:

- **Use a photo when** it sets emotional/human tone the words can't (a hero that makes
  the message felt), shows a product/place/person that must be *seen*, or gives
  editorial credibility (a case study, a story).
- **Do NOT use a photo** as wallpaper behind text "for vibes", to fill an empty band,
  to look busy, or when an icon/shape/gradient conveys the idea more crisply. A
  generic stock-style image reads as filler and fails the critic.

## Rules of thumb

- **One hero image per surface.** Like one dominant element — a single, deliberate
  image, not a scatter of photos. A second image almost always competes.
- **Icons over generated illustrations** for anything iconographic (feature rows,
  checklists, step markers): use the library — reliable and recolorable.
- **Texture/pattern** that sits *behind* content must stay subtle (low contrast,
  scrimmed) so it never fights the text — or use a gradient instead.
- Imagery that genuinely serves the message is welcome; only **gratuitous or cliché**
  imagery is penalized. If you can't name what the image *does* for the message, don't
  generate it.

# Artboard Frame Authoring

Use this reference for every generated exportable artifact.

## Canonical Geometry

Lumen authoring uses canonical layout points (`pt`) for scene geometry:

- A4 portrait preset: about `595 x 842 pt` layout bounds, with print metadata
  of `210mm x 297mm`.
- US Letter: `612 x 792 pt`, with print metadata of `8.5in x 11in`.
- LinkedIn square: `1080 x 1080 pt`, with raster export defaulting to
  `1080 x 1080 px`.
- LinkedIn wide: `1200 x 628 pt`, with raster export defaulting to
  `1200 x 628 px`.
- Custom `6in x 4in`: `432 x 288 pt`, with print metadata of `6in x 4in`.

The agent should author only against layout bounds. Do not use `mm` for child
`p()` or `s()` values. Do not treat renderer pixels as scene coordinates.

Preferred generated structure:

```text
page page_a4 preset(a4,portrait)

      ...

snippets.title: Lumen DSL Vetted Block Catalog
snippets.excerpt:
# Lumen DSL Vetted Block Catalog

A library of pre-proportioned, pre-spaced, **validator-passed** blocks to
**ASSEMBLE** designs from — instead of inventing proportions from primitives every
run (which overcrowds layouts and fails preflight on `LUMV0810`/`0903`/`0904`).
Every fenced `text` example in this folder is a self-contained doc (`page` +
one clipped root `artboard` + the block + `#slot:` fixture lines) that personally
returned `{"ok": true}` from `.context/p02-validate.py`. The only warnings are
`LUMB0613`/`LUMB0614` (platform font not embeddable/subsettable) — environmental,
never failing — plus a non-fatal `LUMV0801` bounds *warning* on the dense A4
one-pager. Use these as the ground truth for correct Lumen DSL syntax + token use.

## Files

| File | Scope |
|------|-------|
| [`patterns.md`](patterns.md) | **Full-artifact compositions** — assemble one of these first, per surface. |
| [`layout.md`](layout.md) | Structural shell blocks — hero, header, footer, divider, section band. |
| [`actions.md`](actions.md) | Buttons, button rows, eyebrows/badges (the calls to action). |
| [`data-display.md`](data-display.md) | Information surfaces — card, stat tile, benefit row/item, logo lockup. |

## Block index

### `patterns.md` — full-artifact compositions (start here)
| Block | Use it for |
|-------|-----------|
| Social square ad (1080×1080) | A square social/display ad: one focal message + 3 proof stats + one CTA. |
| Full-canvas poster (1080×1080) | A LIGHT-content big-canvas ad: one focal message + CTA, no stats, distributed. |
| Image hero (1080×1350) | A **photo-led** editorial hero/poster: full-bleed image + scrim + headline (text-over-image, scrimmed). |
| A4 one-pager (A4 portrait) | A printed/PDF sell-sheet: header + hero + **vertical** 3-up benefits + CTA footer. |
| Landscape flyer (1200×628) | A wide banner/email hero: left message + CTA, right proof-stat panel. |
| Postcard (6×4 in) | The smallest surface: brand + recipient, one headline, one line, one CTA. |

### `layout.md` — structural shell
| Block | Use it for |
|-------|-----------|
| Hero | The single focal message of a social square — eyebrow + headline + subtitle + CTA. |
| Header | Top band of a one-pager: brand lockup left, contact/nav right (`x(sb)`). |
| Footer | Closing band: tinted card with contact + CTA, a rule, and a legal line. |
| Divider | A horizontal rule (a `rect`, since there is no `divider` node); plain or labeled. |
| Section band | A full-bleed tinted band wrapping one focal idea (eyebrow + header + body). |

### `actions.md` — actions
| Block | Use it for |
|-------|-----------|
| Primary CTA button | The single solid, high-contrast primary action of a section. |
| Secondary / outline button | A subordinate action — transparent fill + border, visibly lower priority. |
| Button row | A primary + a fallback action side by side (filled stays dominant). |
| Eyebrow / badge — Variant A (overline) | Default anti-cliche overline above a headline. |
| Eyebrow / badge — Variant B (rule + label) | A short accent rule before the overline label. |
| Eyebrow / badge — Variant C (tinted pill) | Only for genuine status badges ("NOW IN BETA"). |

### `data-display.md` — information surfaces
| Block | Use it for |
|-------|-----------|
| Card | One self-contained idea on a `$surface.card` — title + short paragraph. |
| Stat tile | One spotlight metric — big numeral + short label. Use 1–3, stop at three. |
| Benefit row (3-up) | Three peer benefits **across a wide surface** (1080+); terse descriptions only. |
| Benefit item | One full-width chip + title + description; **stack these** for benefits on A4. |
| Logo lockup | A hero-scale brand identity row — mark + wordmark (`$type.title`). |

## How to compose

1. **Pick a full pattern** from `patterns.md` that matches the requested surface
   (square / A4 / landscape / postcard). It is already correctly proportioned and
   spaced for that surface and has passed the validator.
2. **Swap copy through the `#slot:` lines only.** Edit each slot's `sample(...)` /
   `worst_case(...)`; keep the slotted node's fixed `s(W,H)` unless the worst_case
   grows — if it does, re-validate. Fixtures attach **only** via a
   `#slot:<key> sample("…") worst_case("…")` line indented one level under the
   `page` (never as node properties, never under the artboard).
3. **Swap in component blocks** from `layout.md` / `actions.md` / `data-display.md`
   when you need a region the pattern doesn't have (e.g. drop in a Card, replace a
   solid CTA with a Button row). Keep each component's calibrated `s(W,H)` and the
   shared token choices below so regions line up and stay inside the box.
4. **Respect the content budget** (next section). If content exceeds it, **drop
   content or stack vertically — do not shrink type or cram more in.** Smaller
   surfaces (postcard, flyer) carry *less* content, not the same content smaller.
5. **Re-validate after any structural change** with
   `.context/p02-validate.py`. Ship only what returns `ok==true`.

### Shared token choices (use the same token for the same role)
- Page/one-pager background `$surface.page`; bold hero `$surface.brand`; soft
  tint/chip `$surface.brand.subtle`; card `$surface.card`; quiet band `$surface.muted`.
- **Centering a label (CTA, numeral, monogram, badge):** put it in a container that
  centers on both axes (`al(h, x(c), y(c), ...)`) AND give the LABEL
  `align(center)` + a hug height: `... text "…" s(fill,hug) style($type.x) align(center)`.
  `align(center)` centers the glyph horizontally (the box need NOT hug the glyph);
  the hug height + the container's `y(c)` center it vertically. Do NOT use a hug
  WIDTH (`s(hug,…)`) — it trips a `LUMV0902` re-measure false-overflow.
- CTA button: `fill($surface.inverse)` + `rd($radius.button)`, a fixed-size
  `al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(...))` pill with an `s(fill,hug) align(center)` label.
- Number/initial chip: `$surface.brand.subtle` + `rd($radius.full)` on a fixed-size
  `al(x(c), y(c))` circle, with an `s(fill,hug) align(center)` glyph.
- Brand name in a header/footer band → `$type.label`; standalone hero identity →
  `$type.title` (Logo lockup). Eyebrow → `$type.eyebrow` `max_lines(1)`. Hero/section
  header (5–6 words) → `$type.headline` (not `$type.title`, which won't wrap).
- **Step the hero size to the surface.** `$type.headline` defaults to 56 (right for A4).
  On a large canvas keep the role but override the size with a step token so the headline
  dominates: `style($type.headline) font_size($type.size.6xl)` (64) on a landscape flyer,
  `font_size($type.size.7xl)` (80) on a 1080² square. Steps run `$type.size.xs`(12) →
  `9xl`(128); the role still supplies weight/color, and the size is a fixed value (no
  auto-scaling, so a human editor can resize freely). One element dominates per artifact;
  the hero must read visibly larger than any `$type.stat` (48) value.
- Body copy at print/narrow widths (≤~620pt) → `$type.body.small`; reserve
  `$type.body` for the wide square hero column.
- Divider rule = a `rect` `r s(fill,2) fill($border.subtle)` (numeric thickness —
  `$stroke.width.divider` is illegal inside `s(...)`).
- Personalized account/advertiser values live in the `account.*` slot namespace
  (`account.name`, `account.contact`, …); campaign/offer copy in `campaign.*` /
  `offer.*`; indexed peers in `benefit.N.*` / `stat.N.*`.
- Spacing rhythm: `g($space.section)` between major regions, `g($space.stack.loose)`
  between list rows, `g($space.stack.default)` between peers (headline→subtitle→CTA),
  `g($space.stack.tight)` for label→value (eyebrow→title, value→caption). Outer
  margin `pad(96)` (1080 square) / `pad(48)` (A4) / per-surface for flyer/postcard.

## Composition discipline (the whole point of the catalog)

- **One dominant focal region per artifact**; secondary regions are visibly
  subordinate (smaller type, lighter color, no competing CTA).
- **Aim for ~60–70% whitespace** with generous outer padding. Uncrowded reads as
  intentional and on-brand; dense reads as AI-generated and fails preflight.
- **One CTA per section/artifact.** A second action, if any, is an outline button.
- **Content budget (keeps it uncrowded AND keeps worst_case fixtures in the box):**
  eyebrow 2–4 words `max_lines(1)`; headline 4–8 words `max_lines(2)`; subtitle/lead
  6–12 words `max_lines(2–3)`; body 12–25 words `max_lines(3)`; benefit title ≤4
  words (≤2 ideal) `max_lines(1)`; benefit description ≤12 words `max_lines(2–3)`;
  CTA label 2–3 words `max_lines(1)`; stat = one numeral + ≤2-word label.
- **Never overcrowd.** Never more than 3 benefits in a row, and **on a portrait
  page never 3 *across*** — three description columns can't clear the body-text
  width floor at 595pt and you get guaranteed `LUMV0810`. Stack benefits vertically
  (full-width Benefit item rows) or use a 2-up. Prefer information on surfaces over
  boxing everything in cards. Build hierarchy with size + weight + color, not by
  cramming more elements in.

snippets.excerpt:
# Lumen DSL Vetted Blocks — Layout & Structure

Pre-proportioned, pre-spaced structural blocks for the page shell: hero, header,
footer, divider, and section band. ASSEMBLE these — do not re-invent proportions
from primitives (that is what overcrowds designs and trips `LUMV0810`/`0903`/`0904`).

Every fenced `text` example below is **self-contained** (a `page` + one clipped
root `artboard` + the block + `#slot:` fixture lines) and was personally run
through `.context/p02-validate.py` returning `{"ok": true}`. The only warnings are
`LUMB0613`/`LUMB0614` (platform font not embeddable/subsettable) — environmental,
never failing. Geometry rules that make these pass (calibrated, not guessed):

- A **slotted** text node needs a fixed `s(W,…)` width sized for its `worst_case`
  copy; its **height hugs** (`s(W,hug)`) — `text_fit` now uses the node's own line
  height, so hug heights validate for slotted nodes and reserve no dead space.
  Fixtures attach ONLY via a `#slot:<key> sample(...) worst_case(...)` line indented
  one level under the `page` — never as node properties.
- Width floors (platform type is large): `$type.subtitle` 2 words `ml(1)` ≥ 160;
  `$type.body.small` ~5-word sentence ≥ 220; a 5-6-word header needs `$type.headline`
  at W≥499 (`$type.title` will not wrap 5-6 words at that width).
- A4 portrait is `595 x 842 pt`. With `pad(48)` the content width is `499`; a
  full-bleed band laid in a `pad(0)` artboard is `595` wide and gets `499` of inner
  content width back from its own `pad(48)`. Size slotted text to that `499`.
- Centered labels use `align(center)` + a hug height. A centered container
  (`al(…, x(c), y(c))`) centers the text BOX, but a left-anchored glyph in a box
  wider than itself hugs the left edge — so the text node itself needs
  `align(center)` (alias `text_align(center)`), which sets `text-anchor=middle`
  independently of `style($type.x)`. Keep the label fill-width or a fixed width (do
  NOT use hug WIDTH — it trips `LUMV0902`) and let `align(center)` center the glyph;
  pair it with a hug HEIGHT (`s(fill,hug)`) so the container's `y(c)` centers the
  glyph-tall box. This is how you center a label in a button/chip/cell. Leave
  left-aligned body/title text alone (no `align`).
  A divider is a `rect` (`r s(fill,2) fill($border.subtle)`) — there is no `divider`
  node, and `$stroke.width.divider` is illegal inside `s(...)`.

---

## Hero (eyebrow + headline + subtitle + CTA)

**When to use:** the single focal message of a social square (1080×1080). One
eyebrow, one headline, one supporting sentence, one CTA — vertically centered with
`y(c)` and surrounded by `pad(96)` (~65% whitespace). This is the dominant region;
nothing competes with it.

**When to use / Content budget:** eyebrow 2-4 words `max_lines(1)`; headline 4-8
words `max_lines(2)` at `$type.headline` `lh(1.08)`; subtitle 6-25 words
`max_lines(3)` at `$type.body` `lh(1.4)`; CTA 2-3 words `max_lines(1)`. All four
text nodes are slotted with a fixed worst_case WIDTH and a hug HEIGHT: headline
`888×hug`, subtitle `820×hug`, eyebrow `888×hug` — text heights hug so no dead
space is reserved. The eyebrow/headline/subtitle are left-aligned (`x(s)` column),
so they carry no `align`. The CTA label is `s(fill,hug) align(center)` inside a
fixed `s(340,72)` button (`fill($surface.inverse)` `rd($radius.button)`): the
button's `al(h, x(c), y(c), …)` centers the hug-height label box, and
`align(center)` centers the glyph within it. Hero surface is `$surface.brand`;
the dark button sits on it as the focal action.

```text
page hero_square size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.stack.loose), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.brand) clip(true)
    content al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      eyebrow text "FOR SPECIALTY CLINICS" p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.eyebrow) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.eyebrow)
      headline text "Answer every patient call." p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.08) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
      subtitle text "Insight Health handles intake." p(0,0) s(820,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(offer.primary_message)
      cta al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(18,36)) p(0,0) s(340,72) fill($surface.inverse) rd($radius.button)
        cta_text text "Book a Demo" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.cta) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta)
  #slot:campaign.eyebrow sample("FOR SPECIALTY CLINICS") worst_case("FOR HIGH-VOLUME SPECIALTY CLINICS")
  #slot:campaign.headline sample("Answer every patient call.") worst_case("Give your specialists their operating hours back.")
  #slot:offer.primary_message sample("Insight Health handles intake.") worst_case("Insight Health answers, qualifies, books the visit, and routes the rest to your team.")
  #slot:campaign.cta sample("Book a Demo") worst_case("Start Free Trial")
```

```

---

## Header (logo lockup left + contact/nav right)

**When to use:** the top band of a one-pager / letter. A `space_between`
(`x(sb)`) row: brand lockup pinned left, a single contact or nav line pinned
right, vertically centered with `y(c)`. Keep it visually subordinate to the hero
below it — small type, one line each, no card.

**When to use / Content budget:** wordmark ≤2 words `max_lines(1)` at
`$type.label` (the canonical brand-name role across the catalog; the standalone
**Logo lockup** uses larger `$type.title` only because it is a hero-scale identity
unit) in a `200`-wide box; contact ≤1 line `max_lines(1)` at `$type.body.small` in
a `220`-wide box (the body.small floor); both wordmark and contact use a hug
height (`s(200,hug)`, `s(220,hug)`).
The logo mark is a fixed `s(40,40)` chip (`fill($surface.brand)`
`rd($radius.badge)`) with a 2-letter monogram: the chip's own `al(x(c),y(c))`
centers the label box, and the monogram is `s(fill,hug) align(center)` so the
glyph sits dead-center.
The outer row is fixed `s(499,hug)` (A4 `pad(48)` content width) so the
left/right ends resolve; the brand lockup is a fixed `s(260,hug)` so the
`x(sb)` split is stable.

```text
page header_page preset(a4,portrait)
  artboard al(v, x(s), g($space.section), pad(48)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    header al(h, x(sb), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,hug)
      brand al(h, x(s), y(c), g(12), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(260,hug)
        mark al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(40,40) fill($surface.brand) rd($radius.badge)
          markt text "IH" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.eyebrow) max_lines(1)
        wordmark text "Insight Health" p(0,0) s(200,hug) style($type.label) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.name)
      contact text "hello@insighthealth.com" p(0,0) s(220,hug) style($type.body.small) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.contact)
  #slot:account.name sample("Insight Health") worst_case("Insight Health")
  #slot:account.contact sample("hello@insighthealth.com") worst_case("hello@insighthealth.com")
```

{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Footer (contact + legal, tinted band)

**When to use:** the closing band of a one-pager. A tinted card
(`fill($surface.muted)` `rd($radius.card)` `pad($space.card.padding)`) holding a
`space_between` top row (contact block left, one CTA right), a hairline `rect`
rule, and a fine-print legal line. Visually quiet — it closes the page, it does
not compete with the hero.

**When to use / Content budget:** company name ≤2 words `max_lines(1)`
`$type.label` (matches the Header wordmark and the composition logos); contact line ≤1 short line — but email + phone together exceeds
the body.small 1-line floor, so give it `max_lines(2)` with a `300`-wide hug-height
box; legal ≤15 words `max_lines(2)` at `$type.legal`. All three of these are
left-aligned text in `x(s)` columns, so their heights hug and they carry no
`align`. The CTA is a compact fixed `s(150,56)` button whose label is
`s(fill,hug) align(center)` — the button's `al(h, x(c), y(c), …)` centers the
hug-height box and `align(center)` centers the glyph. The top row is fixed
`s(467,hug)` (the card's inner width:
`499 − 2×16` card padding); contact column `300`, CTA `150` plus the `$space.md`
gap split by `x(sb)`. The rule is `r s(fill,2) fill($border.subtle)` — numeric
height, never `$stroke.width.divider` in `s(...)`.

```text
page footer_page preset(a4,portrait)
  artboard al(v, x(s), g($space.section), pad(48)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    footer al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad($space.card.padding)) p(0,0) s(499,hug) fill($surface.muted) rd($radius.card)
      top al(h, x(sb), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(467,hug)
        contact al(v, x(s), g(4), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(300,hug)
          cname text "Insight Health" p(0,0) s(300,hug) style($type.label) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(account.name)
          cinfo text "hello@insighthealth.com  ·  (555) 012-3456" p(0,0) s(300,hug) style($type.body.small) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(account.contact)
        cta al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(14,28)) p(0,0) s(150,56) fill($surface.inverse) rd($radius.button)
          ctat text "Get Started" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.cta) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta)
      rule r p(0,0) s(fill,2) fill($border.subtle)
      legal text "© 2026 Insight Health, Inc. All rights reserved." p(0,0) s(467,hug) style($type.legal) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(footer.legal)
  #slot:account.name sample("Insight Health") worst_case("Insight Health")
  #slot:account.contact sample("hello@insighthealth.com  ·  (555) 012-3456") worst_case("hello@insighthealth.com  ·  (555) 012-3456")
  #slot:campaign.cta sample("Get Started") worst_case("Get Started")
  #slot:footer.legal sample("© 2026 Insight Health, Inc. All rights reserved.") worst_case("© 2026 Insight Health, Inc. All rights reserved.")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Divider (horizontal rule via rect)

**When to use:** to separate two regions. There is NO `divider` node (`LUMD0206`)
— a rule is a `rect` (`r`) with a numeric thickness: `r s(fill,2)
fill($border.subtle)`. Two forms are shown: a plain full-width rule, and a
labeled rule (rule + centered word + rule) for an "OR"-style break.

**When to use / Content budget:** the rule thickness is the literal number `2`
inside `s(fill,2)` — `$stroke.width.divider` is a `stroke(...)` token only and is
rejected inside `s(...)` (`LUMB0301`). The label in the labeled form is a short,
hard-coded structural word (e.g. "OR") so it carries NO `slot(...)` — give it a
fixed-width hug-height box with `align(center)` (`s(60,hug) align(center)`)
centered in an `al(h, x(c), y(c), …)` between two `r s(fill,2)` rules: the wrapper
centers the box and `align(center)` centers the glyph so the word sits in the gap.

```text
page divider_page preset(a4,portrait)
  artboard al(v, x(s), g($space.section), pad(48)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    above text "Trusted by specialty clinics nationwide." p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2)
    rule r p(0,0) s(fill,2) fill($border.subtle)
    labeled al(h, x(c), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(499,hug)
      l_left r p(0,0) s(fill,2) fill($border.subtle)
      l_text text "OR" p(0,0) s(60,hug) align(center) style($type.eyebrow) max_lines(1)
      l_right r p(0,0) s(fill,2) fill($border.subtle)
    below text "Talk to our team about a pilot." p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2)
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Section band (full-width tinted band wrapper)

**When to use:** wrap a region in a full-bleed tinted band to set it apart from
the page (e.g. a pilot/CTA section). The artboard is `pad(0)` so the band runs
edge to edge (`s(fill,hug)` = 595 wide on A4); the band supplies its own
`pad($space.section)` (use `pad(48)` for a predictable `499` inner width) and a
soft `fill($surface.brand.subtle)`. It holds an eyebrow + a header + one body
paragraph — one focal idea per band.

**When to use / Content budget:** eyebrow 2-4 words `max_lines(1)`; section header
4-6 SHORT words `max_lines(2)` at `$type.headline` (NOT `$type.title`, which will
not wrap 5-6 words at `499`); body 6-12 words `max_lines(3)` at `$type.body`
`lh(1.4)`. All slotted text is sized to the `499` inner WIDTH with a hug HEIGHT —
eyebrow `499×hug`, title `499×hug`, body `499×hug` — so heights hug and reserve no
dead space. These are left-aligned in the `x(s)` band column, so they carry no
`align`. Keep the header tight: at `499`/`ml(2)` the headline fits ~6 short words;
a denser 6-word string (long words back to back) can tip to a 3rd line and fail
`LUMV0810` — stay at or below 6 short words, or raise to `max_lines(2)` (the hug
height grows to fit).

```text
page band_page preset(a4,portrait)
  artboard al(v, x(s), g($space.section), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    band al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(48)) p(0,0) s(fill,hug) fill($surface.brand.subtle)
      eyebrow text "PILOT PROGRAM" p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.eyebrow) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(section.eyebrow)
      title text "Try it on your busiest week." p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.12) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(section.title)
      body text "Run a two-week pilot and measure booked visits." p(0,0) s(499,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(section.body)
  #slot:section.eyebrow sample("PILOT PROGRAM") worst_case("PILOT PROGRAM")
  #slot:section.title sample("Try it on your busiest week.") worst_case("Try it on your busiest week.")
  #slot:section.body sample("Run a two-week pilot and measure booked visits.") worst_case("Run a two-week pilot and measure booked visits.")
```
