snippets.excerpt:
# Lumen DSL Vetted Blocks — Actions (buttons, button rows, eyebrows/badges)

Pre-proportioned, pre-spaced action blocks. ASSEMBLE these — do not re-invent
proportions from primitives. Every fenced `text` example below was personally run
through `.context/p02-validate.py` and returned `{"ok": true}` (only the
environmental `LUMB0613`/`LUMB0614` font warnings remain — those never fail a
block).

Shared rules these blocks encode (so the agent stops overcrowding and stops
failing `LUMV0902/0903/0904`):

- A button is a **fixed-width `al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(...))`** with a single label
  child sized `s(fill,hug) align(center)`. The container's `al(x(c),y(c))` centers
  the label BOX; `align(center)` (alias `text_align(center)`) centers the GLYPH
  inside that box (text-anchor=middle) so the label sits dead-center even when the
  box is wider than the text. Centered labels use `align(center)` + hug height;
  text heights hug. Keep `style($type.x)` as-is — `align()` is a standalone text
  property that sets horizontal alignment independently of the type role.
- A slotted label takes a **definite width from its fixed-width button** plus a
  **hug height** (`s(fill,hug)` inside a fixed button: the button supplies the
  definite width, `text_fit` hugs the glyph-tall height off the node's own line
  height). Do NOT give a slotted label a hug WIDTH (that trips `LUMV0902`).
- One primary action per section; a secondary action is visibly subordinate
  (outline, not filled). Generous outer padding (`pad(96)` square / `pad(48)`+ A4)
  keeps ~60-70% whitespace.

---

## Primary CTA button

**When to use:** the single primary action of a section/artifact — solid, high
contrast, centered label. Exactly one per section.

**When to use / Content budget:** CTA label 2-3 words, `max_lines(1)`. Solid
`fill($surface.inverse)` (dark button on a light/brand surface), `rd($radius.button)`.
Button is a fixed `s(340,76)` `al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(20,40))`; the label is
`s(fill,hug) align(center)` (fill the button's width, hug the glyph-tall height,
center the glyph) at `style($type.cta)`. Centered labels use `align(center)` + hug
height; text heights hug — the button's `y(c)` vertically centers the hugged box,
and `align(center)` horizontally centers the glyph inside the fill-width box.

```text
page primary_cta_demo size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.stack.loose), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    content al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      headline text "Ready when you are." p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.08) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
      cta al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(20,40)) p(0,0) s(340,76) fill($surface.inverse) rd($radius.button)
        cta_text text "Book a Demo" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.cta) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta)
  #slot:campaign.headline sample("Ready when you are.") worst_case("Ready when you are.")
  #slot:campaign.cta sample("Book a Demo") worst_case("Start Free Trial")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Secondary / outline button

**When to use:** a subordinate action that should not compete with the primary CTA
— a transparent fill with a border, so it reads as visibly lower priority.

**When to use / Content budget:** label 2-3 words, `max_lines(1)`. Transparent fill
via `fill(#00000000)` (fully transparent — there is no `$transparent` token), a
border via `stroke($border.strong, $stroke.width.firm)`, and `rd($radius.button)`.
Stroke-width tokens (`$stroke.width.*`) are valid ONLY inside `stroke(...)`; putting
one inside `s(...)` raises `LUMB0301`. Same fixed `s(340,76)` button geometry and
`s(fill,hug) align(center)` label as the primary, so a primary and a secondary line
up pixel-for-pixel.

```text
page secondary_cta_demo size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.stack.loose), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    content al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      headline text "See it in action first." p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.08) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
      cta al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(20,40)) p(0,0) s(340,76) fill(#00000000) stroke($border.strong, $stroke.width.firm) rd($radius.button)
        cta_text text "Watch the Tour" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.cta) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta)
  #slot:campaign.headline sample("See it in action first.") worst_case("See it in action first.")
  #slot:campaign.cta sample("Watch the Tour") worst_case("Watch the Tour")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Button row (primary + secondary side by side)

**When to use:** a decision point that offers a primary AND a fallback action
(e.g. "Start Free" / "Talk to Sales"). The filled button stays dominant; the
outline button subordinate.

**When to use / Content budget:** each label 2-3 words, `max_lines(1)`. The row is
`al(h, x(s), y(c), g($space.md))` with a fixed width (`888`). Both buttons are
fixed `s(320,76)` so they add up inside the row (320 + 320 + `$space.md` gap < 888)
— give the row a definite width whenever its children are fixed-width, so the math
is checkable. Primary = solid `fill($surface.inverse)`; secondary = transparent
`fill(#00000000)` + `stroke($border.strong, $stroke.width.firm)`. NEVER make both
filled — equal emphasis defeats the hierarchy.

```text
page button_row_demo size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.stack.loose), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    content al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      headline text "Start free or talk to sales." p(0,0) s(888,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.08) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(campaign.headline)
      actions al(h, x(s), y(c), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
        primary al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(20,40)) p(0,0) s(320,76) fill($surface.inverse) rd($radius.button)
          primary_text text "Start Free" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.cta) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta_primary)
        secondary al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(20,40)) p(0,0) s(320,76) fill(#00000000) stroke($border.strong, $stroke.width.firm) rd($radius.button)
          secondary_text text "Talk to Sales" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) align(center) style($type.cta) max_lines(1) slot(campaign.cta_secondary)
  #slot:campaign.headline sample("Start free or talk to sales.") worst_case("Start free or talk to sales.")
  #slot:campaign.cta_primary sample("Start Free") worst_case("Start Free")
  #slot:campaign.cta_secondary sample("Talk to Sales") worst_case("Talk to Sales")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Eyebrow / badge pill (three variants — prefer the non-pill ones)

**When to use:** a small overline above a headline that names the audience, theme,
or status. The tinted pill is an AI cliche — **prefer variant A (plain overline)
or B (rule + label)**; reach for variant C (tinted pill) only when the content is a
genuine status badge ("NOW IN BETA", "NEW").

**When to use / Content budget (all variants):** 2-4 words, ONE short line,
`max_lines(1)`, `style($type.eyebrow)` (small-caps overline). Pair it with the
headline using `g($space.stack.tight)` so the eyebrow reads as attached to the
title. A slotted eyebrow takes a definite width and a hug height (`s(W,hug)`); `W`
is wide because platform type is large (888 for a full-width overline, 420 next to
a rule, `s(fill,hug)` inside a fixed pill). A centered pill label uses
`align(center)` + hug height; left-aligned overlines stay left (no `align`). Keep
the eyebrow visibly subordinate to the headline — it is small caps, not a second
headline.

### Variant A — plain overline (default; no box, the anti-cliche choice)

```text
page eyebrow_overline_demo size(1080,1080,px)
```

# Lumen DSL Vetted Blocks — Data Display

Pre-proportioned, validator-passed building blocks for surfacing information:
cards, stat tiles, benefit rows/items, and a logo lockup. **Assemble** these
instead of inventing proportions from primitives — the sizing below is already
calibrated against the fixture-fit validator so the agent stops overcrowding and
stops failing `LUMV0810`/`LUMV0903`/`LUMV0904`.

Every fenced `text` example is a self-contained doc (`page` + one clipped root
`artboard` + the block + `#slot:` fixture lines) that **personally returned
`ok==true`** from `.context/p02-validate.py`. The only warnings are
`LUMB0613`/`LUMB0614` (platform font not embeddable/subsettable) — these are
environmental and never fail a block.

Universal rules these blocks bake in:

- **Slotted text node ⇒ definite width + HUG height** sized for the `worst_case`
  copy: `s(W,hug)`. `text_fit` uses the node's own line height, so hug heights
  validate for slotted nodes too — a fixed pixel height just reserves dead space.
  Keep the width definite and `wrap_text(true) + max_lines(N)`; let the height hug.
- Fixtures attach **only** via a `#slot:<key> sample("…") worst_case("…")` modify
  line indented one level under the `page` (never under the artboard, never as a
  node property).
- Tokens only — `$surface.*`, `$text.*`, `$type.*`, `$space.*`, `$radius.*`,
  `$border.*`. Colors are never bare numbers; `rd()` is one uniform radius.
- Center a *label's glyph* with `align(center)` (alias `text_align(center)`) on the
  text node — it sets horizontal text alignment independently of `style($type.x)`
  and renders the glyph centered (no hug-width needed). When the label sits in a
  taller centered container (`al(…, x(c), y(c))`), pair `align(center)` with a
  **hug height** (`s(fill,hug) align(center)`) so the container's `y(c)` centers
  the glyph-tall box. Do **not** use hug WIDTH for centering (trips `LUMV0902`).
  Leave left-aligned body/title text alone (keep it left / `x(s)`).

---

## Card

**When to use:** a single self-contained unit of content on a page surface — a
title with a short supporting paragraph — set on `$surface.card`. Reach for this
when one idea deserves a contained, slightly elevated region rather than living
loose on the page. One card is a secondary region; do not tile a page with cards.

**When to use / Content budget:** title ≤4 words `max_lines(2)` (`$type.headline`,
wraps where `$type.title` will not); body 12-25 words `max_lines(3)`
(`$type.body`). The 752pt body column clears the `$type.body` width floor — a
14-word `worst_case` fits in 3 lines at this width; do not push past ~15 words at
`max_lines(3)` or the fixture overflows (`LUMV0810`). Title and body are
left-aligned (`x(s)`), so they keep their definite width with **hug heights**
(`s(752,hug)`) — text heights hug, no dead space reserved. Card is
`pad($space.card.padding)` inside `rd($radius.card)`; title→body gap is
`$space.stack.default`.

```text
page card_demo size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.section), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    card al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.default), pad($space.card.padding)) p(0,0) s(840,hug) fill($surface.card) rd($radius.card)
      card_title text "Automated patient intake" p(0,0) s(752,hug) style($type.headline) lh(1.12) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(card.title)
      card_body text "Insight Health answers, qualifies, and books the visit." p(0,0) s(752,hug) style($type.body) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(card.body)
  #slot:card.title sample("Automated patient intake") worst_case("Automated patient intake")
  #slot:card.body sample("Insight Health answers, qualifies, and books the visit.") worst_case("Insight Health answers, qualifies, books the visit, and routes the rest to your team.")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Stat tile

**When to use:** spotlight one metric — a big number with a short label beneath
it. Use 1-3 of these in a row for social proof / outcomes; stop at three.

**When to use / Content budget:** value 1 short numeral/token `max_lines(1)`
(`$type.stat`); label ≤5 words `max_lines(2)` (`$type.caption`,
`$text.secondary` by default). The value box keeps a definite **356pt width**
with a **hug height** (`s(356,hug)`) so a `worst_case` like `"12,480"` (a count,
not just a percentage) still fits at `$type.stat` — slot the value as `stat.value`
and size the *width* for the *longest* realistic number; the height hugs (no dead
zone). Value and label are left-aligned (`x(s)`), so they stay left — no
`align(center)` here. The tile is `pad($space.card.padding)`; value→label gap is
`$space.stack.tight` (the label reads as a caption *belonging to* the number, so
keep them tight).

```text
page stat_demo size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.section), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    tile al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.tight), pad($space.card.padding)) p(0,0) s(420,hug) fill($surface.card) rd($radius.card)
      stat_value text "98%" p(0,0) s(356,hug) style($type.stat) lh(1.0) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(stat.value)
      stat_label text "of calls answered in seconds" p(0,0) s(356,hug) style($type.caption) lh(1.3) wrap_text(true) max_lines(2) slot(stat.label)
  #slot:stat.value sample("98%") worst_case("12,480")
  #slot:stat.label sample("of calls answered in seconds") worst_case("of calls answered in seconds")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Benefit row (3-up)

**When to use:** three peer benefits *across* a **wide** surface (1080 square or
wider). This is the disciplined horizontal 3-up. **Do not author a 3-across row on
A4 portrait** — at 595pt the three description columns cannot clear the body-text
width floor and you get guaranteed `LUMV0810`; on A4, stack benefits as full-width
rows (use **Benefit item** repeated) instead.

**When to use / Content budget:** title ≤2 words `max_lines(1)` (`$type.subtitle`,
≥160pt box); description **≤6 words** `max_lines(3)` (`$type.body.small`). This is
the key discipline encoded here: at the narrow ~280pt column width of a 3-up,
descriptions MUST be terse — a 10-word description overflows `LUMV0810` even at
`max_lines(6)`. Keep them to a single short phrase. Geometry: 1080 square,
`pad(96)` ⇒ 888pt content; three `s(280,…)` cells + two `g(24)` gaps = 888 exactly.
Titles and descriptions are left-aligned (`x(s)`) and keep their 280pt width with
**hug heights** (`s(280,hug)`) — text heights hug, no dead space. Title→desc gap
is `$space.stack.tight`. If you need richer descriptions, switch to a stacked
layout of **Benefit item** rows (wide columns fit long copy).

```text
page benefit_row_demo size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.section), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    row al(h, x(s), y(s), g(24), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      c1 al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.tight), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(280,hug)
        c1t text "Faster intake" p(0,0) s(280,hug) style($type.subtitle) lh(1.15) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(benefit.1.title)
        c1d text "Route every call in seconds." p(0,0) s(280,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(benefit.1.desc)
      c2 al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.tight), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(280,hug)
        c2t text "Less busywork" p(0,0) s(280,hug) style($type.subtitle) lh(1.15) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(benefit.2.title)
        c2d text "Reminders sent automatically." p(0,0) s(280,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(benefit.2.desc)
      c3 al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.tight), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(280,hug)
        c3t text "Happier patients" p(0,0) s(280,hug) style($type.subtitle) lh(1.15) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(benefit.3.title)
        c3d text "Shorter waits, clearer steps." p(0,0) s(280,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(benefit.3.desc)
  #slot:benefit.1.title sample("Faster intake") worst_case("Faster intake")
  #slot:benefit.1.desc sample("Route every call in seconds.") worst_case("Route every call in seconds.")
  #slot:benefit.2.title sample("Less busywork") worst_case("Less busywork")
  #slot:benefit.2.desc sample("Reminders sent automatically.") worst_case("Reminders sent automatically.")
  #slot:benefit.3.title sample("Happier patients") worst_case("Happier patients")
  #slot:benefit.3.desc sample("Shorter waits, clearer steps.") worst_case("Shorter waits, clearer steps.")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Benefit item

**When to use:** a single icon/number + title + description unit, full width. This
is the row primitive to **stack vertically** when you have 2-4 benefits and want
real descriptions (the correct shape for A4 portrait, where a 3-across row cannot
fit body text — see Benefit row above). Repeat it inside a
`al(v, g($space.stack.loose))` list.

**When to use / Content budget:** title ≤4 words `max_lines(1)` (`$type.subtitle`);
description ≤16 words `max_lines(3)` (`$type.body.small`). Because the copy column
is full-width (792pt here), it clears the body-text floor with room to spare — so
descriptions can be a full sentence, unlike the cramped 3-up. Title and
description are left-aligned (`x(s)`) with **hug heights** (`s(792,hug)`) — text
heights hug, no dead space. The leading chip is a fixed `s(72,72)` `rd($radius.full)`
on `$surface.brand.subtle`; its glyph is centered with `align(center)` + a hug
height (`s(fill,hug) align(center)`) so the chip's `x(c), y(c)` centers the
glyph-tall box (swap the `"1"` for a number, initial, or a `vector`/`svg` icon).
Chip→copy gap is `$space.md`; title→desc gap is `$space.stack.tight`.

```text
page benefit_item_demo size(1080,1080,px)
  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.section), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    item al(h, x(s), y(s), g($space.md), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(888,hug)
      icon al(h, x(c), y(c), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(72,72) fill($surface.brand.subtle) rd($radius.full)
        glyph text "1" p(0,0) s(fill,hug) style($type.title) align(center) max_lines(1)
      copy al(v, x(s), g($space.stack.tight), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(792,hug)
        item_title text "Answer every call" p(0,0) s(792,hug) style($type.subtitle) lh(1.15) wrap_text(true) max_lines(1) slot(benefit.title)
        item_desc text "Insight Health picks up day or night, qualifies the patient, and books the visit automatically." p(0,0) s(792,hug) style($type.body.small) lh(1.4) wrap_text(true) max_lines(3) slot(benefit.desc)
  #slot:benefit.title sample("Answer every call") worst_case("Answer every call")
  #slot:benefit.desc sample("Insight Health picks up day or night, qualifies the patient, and books the visit automatically.") worst_case("Insight Health picks up day or night, qualifies the patient, and books the visit automatically.")
```

Validator proof:
```json
{ "ok": true, "stage": "preflight", "errors": [], "warnings": ["LUMB0613", "LUMB0614"] }
```

---

## Logo lockup

**When to use:** a brand identity row — a mark next to a wordmark — for a header,
footer, or proof region. The wordmark is the place to slot a personalized account
name.

**When to use / Content budget:** wordmark ≤3 words `max_lines(1)` (`$type.title`,
*not* `$type.headline` — title is the right scale for a wordmark and stays robust
for longer account names: a 23-char `worst_case` like `"Riverside Medical Group"`
fits at the 480pt-wide box). The wordmark is left-aligned (`x(s)`) and keeps its
480pt width with a **hug height** (`s(480,hug)`) — text height hugs, no dead space.
The mark is a fixed `s(64,64)` chip on `$surface.brand` with `rd($radius.md)`; its
glyph is centered with `align(center)` + a hug height (`s(fill,hug) align(center)`)
so the chip's `x(c), y(c)` centers the glyph-tall box (swap `"IH"` for an
`image asset(...)` logo or a `vector`/`svg` mark). The row is `y(c)` so mark and
wordmark are vertically centered; mark→wordmark gap is `$space.sm` (a lockup reads
as one unit, so keep the gap tight).

```text

  artboard al(v, x(s), y(c), g($space.section), pad(96)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    lockup al(h, x(s), y(c), g($space.sm), pad(0)) p(0,0) s(560,hug)
```

---
# Imagery — Prompt Craft (the 5-component structure)

Once `knowledge/images/decide` says "generate a photo", write the prompt well. A vague
keyword bag ("business, technology, success, blue") produces generic stock-feel
filler. Specificity is what makes a generated image look art-directed. Every
`asset(action="generate_image")` prompt carries **five components**, in descriptive prose.

## The five components

1. **Subject** — what is literally in frame, concretely. *Who/what, doing what,
   where.* "A focused neurosurgeon reviewing a glowing 3D brain scan on a translucent
   display" — not "doctor, technology".
2. **Medium / Style** — name the medium: *editorial photograph*, *cinematic still*,
   *3D render*, *watercolor illustration*, *flat vector-style illustration*,
   *macro photograph*. This sets the whole look.
3. **Composition** — framing + angle + depth: *wide establishing shot*, *tight
   portrait*, *overhead flat-lay*, *shallow depth of field*, *subject off to one
   side*. If text will overlay the image, **compose for it** (see below).
4. **Lighting** — quality + direction + mood: *soft window light*, *dramatic side
   light*, *golden-hour backlight*, *clean studio softbox*, *moody low-key*.
5. **Quality / Render cues** — *high detail*, *premium*, *editorial*, *muted
   palette*, *photorealistic*. Keep these few and purposeful, not a pile of buzzwords.

Write them as one or two natural sentences, not a comma list. Prose beats keywords.

## Hard rules

- **No in-image text.** Models garble lettering, and all real copy comes from the
  design layer (it must be editable + on-brand). End every prompt with *"no text, no
  words, no letters, no logos, no watermarks."*
- **Brand tone goes in `brand_notes`, not the prompt.** Pass palette + mood as
  `brand_notes` (e.g. `["deep navy + teal palette", "calm clinical confidence",
  "premium, uncluttered"]`). The model conditions on them; the prompt stays about the
  scene.
- **Compose for the overlay.** If text/scrim will sit on the image, prompt for a clean
  area: *"ample uncluttered negative space in the lower third for text"*, *"subject on
  the right, soft empty background on the left."* This is what makes a scrimmed hero
  read cleanly (see `knowledge/images/placement`).
- **Aspect comes from the frame, not the prompt.** `asset(action="generate_image")` derives
  the aspect ratio from the target node's geometry — don't hardcode a ratio that fights the frame.

## Per-use-case templates

Fill the five components into the right skeleton:

- **Hero (full-bleed, text overlays):** `<editorial/cinematic photograph> of <subject + action + setting>, <composition with negative space for text>, <lighting + mood>, premium, no text.`
- **Product:** `<studio/editorial photograph> of <product>, <angle — three-quarter / overhead>, on <clean surface>, soft studio lighting, crisp detail, no text.`
- **Portrait / person:** `<natural editorial portrait> of <person + role + expression>, <framing — head-and-shoulders / environmental>, soft directional light, shallow depth of field, no text.`
- **Food:** `<appetizing overhead/45° photograph> of <dish>, natural soft light, fresh ingredients, shallow depth of field, no text.`
- **Texture / background:** `<macro photograph or abstract render> of <material/pattern>, even soft light, subtle and low-contrast (it sits behind content), no text.`
- **Illustration (raster):** `<flat / isometric / watercolor> illustration of <concept>, <limited brand-aligned palette>, clean composition, no text.` (For *icons* or simple flat marks use the library — `svg(icon:name)` — not the model; see `knowledge/images/decide`.)

assumes: images/decide, assets/asset-placement

# Imagery — Placement & the Scrim Rule

How a generated or library image goes into a design. Two non-negotiables: an image is
placed **onto a target frame** (the frame's geometry drives the aspect, the image is
cropped to fill — never stretched), and **text over an image always gets a scrim**
beneath it for legibility. Both examples below were run through `.context/p02-validate.py`
and return `{"ok": true}` (only the platform-font warnings `LUMB0613`/`LUMB0614`).

Builds on `knowledge/images/decide` (decide *whether* a surface earns an image first)
and `knowledge/assets/asset-placement` (the asset-registry rules + the
`place_asset_in_node` / `place_asset_in_slot` op contract this placement compiles to).

## Place onto a target — cover + focal, never stretched

- The image fills a frame whose **aspect comes from the frame**, not the image. The
  agent tool `asset(action="generate_image", target_node_id=…)` derives the ratio from the
  target's geometry; `asset(action="place", node_id=…/slot_id=…)` then drops the asset in.
- **Default `fit:cover` + a focal point.** Cover crops to fill the frame at the image's
  natural ratio; the focal point (0..1, default centered) keeps the subject in view —
  raise it for faces/upper subjects, bias it toward the busy side. Never `fill`-stretch
  a photo (distorts), never letterbox a hero (dead bands).
- Always set **alt text** describing the image.
- Clip the frame (`clip(true)`) and round it (`rd($radius.card)`) when the design wants
  rounded imagery; the image is clipped to the frame.

## The scrim rule — text over image is ALWAYS scrimmed

A scrim is a semi-transparent rectangle **between the image and the text**, using the
`$opacity.scrim` (0.56) or `$opacity.overlay` (0.88) token. Dark scrim
(`$surface.inverse`) under **light** text (`$text.inverse`); or a light scrim under
dark text. Without it, text on a photo is illegible the moment the photo is busy —
this is the single most common imagery failure the critic rejects.

**Make the artboard a dark surface (`fill($surface.inverse)`).** Brand tokens resolve
*relative to their container's surface*: on a dark artboard `$text.inverse` and the
`$type.*` roles resolve to **light** ink (legible over the scrim); on a light
`$surface.page` artboard the *same* tokens resolve **dark** and the headline goes invisible
against the photo. So a full-bleed-photo surface is a **dark** surface — and the dark fill
doubles as the fallback colour if the image fails to load.

### Idiom A — full-bleed image + scrim + text (the hero)

Image fills the artboard; a scrim sits on top; text is anchored at the bottom over the
scrim. Declaration order is z-order: image, then scrim, then text.

```text
page hero size(1080,1350,px)
  artboard fr p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.inverse) clip(true)
    photo image asset(hero_photo) p(0,0) s(1080,1350)
    scrim r p(0,0) s(1080,1350) fill($surface.inverse) o($opacity.scrim)
    content al(v,x(s),y(e),g($space.stack.tight),pad($space.card.padding)) p(0,0) s(1080,1350)
      kicker text "CASE STUDY" p(0,0) s(936,40) style($type.label) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true)
      headline text "Faster triage, calmer clinics" p(0,0) s(936,240) style($type.headline) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true)
```

### Idiom B — split: image region + text on its own surface (no scrim needed)

When text sits on its own band rather than on the photo, **no scrim is needed** — the
text is on a solid surface, not the image. Safer than a scrim when legibility is
critical. Image hero on top, a brand band below absorbs the slack and centers its copy.

```text
page hero size(1080,1350,px)
  artboard al(v,x(s),g(0),pad(0)) p(0,0) s(fill,fill) fill($surface.page) clip(true)
    photo image asset(hero_photo) p(0,0) s(1080,810)
    band al(v,x(s),y(c),g($space.stack.tight),pad($space.card.padding)) p(0,0) s(1080,fill) fill($surface.brand)
      kicker text "CASE STUDY" p(0,0) s(936,40) style($type.label) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true)
      headline text "Faster triage, calmer clinics" p(0,0) s(936,200) style($type.headline) fill($text.inverse) wrap_text(true)
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Image placed onto a frame, aspect from the frame, `fit:cover` + focal point.
- [ ] Text over the image? A scrim rect sits beneath the text (Idiom A) — or move the
      text to its own surface (Idiom B).
- [ ] Text color contrasts the scrim/surface (`$text.inverse` on a dark scrim).
- [ ] Alt text set; one hero image per surface; nothing stretched.

# Imagery — Icons (the reliable vector path)

For anything **iconographic** — feature rows, checklists, step markers, bullet accents,
directional cues — reach for a **library icon**, not `asset(action="generate_image")`. A curated vector is
reliable, crisp at any size, and recolors to brand; a model garbles small flat marks. This
is the `icon → library` branch of `knowledge/images/decide`.

## How to place an icon

Use `svg(icon:NAME)` as the element kind, size the node, and recolor with a `fill(...)`
token (every icon is a filled shape, so `fill` is the color):

```text
mark svg(icon:check) p(0,0) s(28,28) fill($surface.brand)
```

- **Size the node** (`s(W,H)`) — the icon scales uniformly to fit and centers in the box.
  No need to match a 24px source; a `s(48,48)` node renders a 48px icon.
- **Recolor with `fill($color.* / $surface.* / $text.*)`** — keep icons on one brand color,
  not a rainbow. For an icon sitting on a brand surface, use `fill($text.inverse)`.
- **One consistent icon style per surface.** Don't mix an icon row with a generated
  illustration; pick the library for the whole set so they read as a family.
- **Icon + label** pattern: a small horizontal `al(h, x(s), y(c), g(...))` row with the icon
  then a text label; repeat for a feature/checklist/step row.

## Available icons (Slice 0 curated set)

Geometric / markers: `circle`, `dot`, `square`, `diamond`, `triangle-up`, `play`, `star`,
`heart`, `bolt`.
Status / actions: `check`, `x`, `plus`, `minus`.
Directional (block arrows): `arrow-right`, `arrow-left`, `arrow-up`, `arrow-down`.

An unknown name fails compile (`LUMD0703`) and the error lists the valid options — pick the
closest shipped icon (e.g. `check` for "done", `bolt` for "fast", `star` for "featured",
`arrow-right` for "next"/"learn more") rather than inventing a name. The set is curated and
extensible; richer pictograms (calendar, shield, users…) arrive in a later slice.

## When NOT to use an icon

- A **photo/portrait/product** that must be seen → `asset(action="generate_image")` (see `images/decide`).
- A **logo** → a brand `logo.*` / `asset.*` token, never `svg(icon:...)`; for the logo
  roles + allowed-surface rules see `knowledge/design-systems/logo-and-assets`.
- Pure **decoration that adds no meaning** → drop it; whitespace beats clutter.

snippets.excerpt:
# Asset Placement Guidance

Status: supported now, recognized but not lowered, and future scaffold.

Related: `knowledge/images/placement` (the cover/focal-point + text-over-image scrim
idioms for placing a hero image) and `knowledge/design-systems/logo-and-assets` (brand
logo/asset roles + allowed-surface rules).

## Supported Now

Agents may reference registered or fixture assets by stable asset IDs. Use
assets for logos, hero images, icons, and vector marks only when the scene asset
registry contains the referenced asset.

Good pattern:

```text
logo image asset(account_logo) p(32,32) s(96,48) slot(account.logo)
```

Asset placement should respect:

- aspect ratio
- crop/fit policy
- minimum readable size
- enough whitespace around logos
- provenance/licensing metadata in the asset record

## Recognized But Not Lowered

The current Phase A runtime does not own real upload, storage, provider image
generation, vectorization, or production asset processing. If the user request
requires a missing image, the agent should request/select a fixture asset or
record an asset gap.

## Future Scaffold

Future asset work should add:

- upload/import API
- object storage
- image probing and thumbnails
- generation/vectorization providers
- asset search
- export-time byte resolution and embedding
